signature.name: Universal Studios Hollywood
signature.detail: The world's first Universal park and a must for movie fans, combining a working studio tour with major rides. Buy tickets online in advance and arrive at opening to beat the queues; it is in Universal City, reachable by Metro B Line.

signature.name: Hollywood Sign
signature.detail: The most recognizable symbol of the film industry, best seen from Griffith Park or the Lake Hollywood area. Go early in the morning for clear light and fewer crowds; there is no parking at the sign itself, so hike or view from a distance.

signature.name: Griffith Observatory
signature.detail: A free public observatory with sweeping views over Los Angeles and the Hollywood Sign. Entry is free but planetarium shows are ticketed; visit at sunset for the best light and check opening days, as it is closed on some weekdays.

signature.name: Santa Monica Pier
signature.detail: A classic seaside pier with an amusement park, aquarium and ocean views at the end of Route 66. It is free to walk on; ride the Ferris wheel at sunset and take the Metro E Line to Downtown Santa Monica.

signature.name: Hollywood Walk of Fame
signature.detail: The famous sidewalk of celebrity stars along Hollywood Boulevard, free to stroll. Come early or on a weekday to avoid crowds, and combine it with the TCL Chinese Theatre next door.

signature.name: The Getty Center
signature.detail: A hilltop art museum with world-class collections, gardens and panoramic city views. Admission is free; pay only for parking, and take the tram up from the garage.

signature.name: Venice Beach
signature.detail: A lively boardwalk with street performers, muscle beach and canals nearby. Rent a bike to ride to Santa Monica; weekends are busiest, so go on a weekday morning.

signature.name: TCL Chinese Theatre
signature.detail: Historic movie palace famous for its forecourt of celebrity handprints and footprints. The forecourt is free to visit; book a movie ticket to see the ornate interior.

transport: Metro $1.75 a ride; rideshares $15-30 across town
